headline: Strategists at Bank of America say that buying shares in companies that benefit from AI spending is no longer an easy way to make money.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a large US bank's strategists say the AI-spending bet is crowded, but it is one team's reading of fund positioning, not a forecast of falling prices.
importance_line: Savers in share funds and the fund managers who run them may find the AI-spending favourites harder to profit from, but this is one bank's reading of investor positions, not a prediction that prices will fall.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by AdvisorHub, that Bank of America strategists led by Savita Subramanian wrote on Monday that investors will find it harder to make "easy money" by betting on companies that gain from AI spending rather than on consumer spending, because both trends are already built into investor positions. The note says long-only active funds hold near-record-low positions in software, IT services and consumer finance companies, which it calls "AI disruptees", and Subramanian called that positioning "justified".
